title: An AI-Powered Mobile Application for Intelligent Personal Finance Management and Decision Support
venue: International Journal of Recent Trends in Technology and Engineering (IJRTTE), 03(03)
tldr: Proposes an AI-enabled mobile app using Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and Reinforcement Learning with NLP for personalized, secure personal finance management and decision support.
problem_and_motivation: Existing personal finance management systems lack personalization, fail to adapt to changing data, lack predictive capabilities, and inadequately address security and privacy. They predominantly rely on rule-based or simplistic statistical methods that cannot cope with varied financial behavior and changing markets.
approach: Designed a five-layer modular architecture: User Interface, Data Acquisition, Data Processing/Feature Engineering, AI/Decision Support, and Security/Compliance.
Used Random Forest for expense prediction, XGBoost for cashflow forecasting, LSTM for time-series modeling, and Reinforcement Learning for adaptive goal tracking.
Integrated NLP using BERT-based transformer models for conversational financial coaching and educational modules via chatbot.
Implemented federated learning with differential privacy for privacy-preserving collaborative model training across user devices.
Applied feature engineering to compute Income Stability Index, Expenditure Volatility Score, Debt-to-Income ratio, and Investment Diversification Index.
Built cross-platform mobile app using Flutter with TensorFlow Lite for on-device ML inference and secure API integrations.
Used AWS/GCP cloud services with PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and InfluxDB databases orchestrated via Docker and Kubernetes.
Evaluated on anonymized financial records from 500 users over 12 months with 150-participant user study.
findings: num: Goal Alignment Accuracy of 92.5%, Expense Categorization Accuracy of 96.8%, User-specific Budget Optimization Accuracy of 91.2%.
num: Forecasting R² scores of 0.93 (income), 0.91 (expenses), and 0.89 (savings) demonstrating strong predictive accuracy.
num: User satisfaction rated at 94% highly satisfied, with 92% finding the interface intuitive and 89% reporting improved financial control.
num: 91% of users expressed confidence in AI-generated financial recommendations.
Proposed system outperformed existing platforms across all criteria including real-time data integration, personalization, predictive analytics, and risk assessment.
Comparative analysis showed existing systems averaged 75-80% user satisfaction versus 94% for the proposed system.
AES-256 encryption, GDPR/PCI DSS compliance, and multi-factor authentication ensured robust data security.
Federated learning approach enabled privacy-preserving model training without centralized data pooling.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides an integrated AI-powered mobile platform combining multiple ML algorithms, real-time data integration, NLP-based financial literacy, and privacy-preserving federated learning into a unified personal finance management system.
directly_justifies: Odin's use of Random Forest and LSTM models for financial forecasting and budget optimization.
Integration of real-time data processing and secure financial data handling.
Mobile-based financial management interface with personalized recommendations.
limits: Focuses on individual personal finance, not tested on business or SME financial management.
Model evaluated on only 500 anonymized users over 12 months; larger-scale deployment needed.
No implementation details for behavioral economics integration or social media sentiment analysis.
Relies on simulated/prototype environment rather than real-world longitudinal deployment.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Paper describes an algorithmic system for personal finance management using AI/ML, covering budgeting, forecasting, goal tracking, security, and user interface design.

limitations: System primarily targets individual personal finance; not extended to small or large business finance management.
Evaluation limited to 500 users from a single geographic region; lacks geographical, cultural, and socio-economic diversity.
No longitudinal large-scale real-world deployment to verify long-term stability and sustained user engagement.
Potential expert selection bias and limited data types in the Ploutos-like recommendation framework.
